title: Event settings
goal: Create a group, change its settings, and count the days left.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• create_group(db, name, kind, budget, deadline): return the new id. The name is stripped. ValueError for an empty name, a kind that is not work, family or friends, a negative budget, or a deadline that is not a real ISO date such as 2026-12-20.
  • update_group(db, group_id, name, budget, deadline): same validation.
  • days_left(deadline, today=None): whole days until the deadline, negative if it has passed. today defaults to the real date.
  • deadline_status(deadline, today=None): "late" if passed, "soon" if 7 days or less, otherwise "ok".

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A form to edit the selected group, a countdown metric with a warning when the deadline is soon or late, and a form to create a new group (after creating it, st.rerun() so the sidebar shows it).

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: datetime.date.fromisoformat, and subtracting two dates gives a timedelta with .days. Today is "soon", not "late".

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: A progress bar from the creation date to the deadline. Delete a group (with confirmation).

title: Participants
goal: Add, list and remove the people of a group.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• add_participant(db, group_id, name, email): add the person and return the new id. Spaces around the name are removed and the email is lowercased. Raise ValueError for an empty name, an email without @, or an email already in this group (the same email is allowed in another group).
  • list_participants(db, group_id): the people of this group only, sorted by name.
  • delete_participant(db, participant_id): remove the person. Their group's draw becomes invalid, so it is cancelled too (delete the group's rows in assignments).

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A form (name, email), a counter of participants, the list with a delete button for each person.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: str.strip() and str.lower(). To refuse a duplicate, ask exists(...) first, then insert(...). When someone is deleted, find their group with find_one(...) before deleting them. After a delete, st.rerun() refreshes the list. Use st.form so the page does not rerun on every keystroke.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Edit a participant. Search box. Ask for confirmation before deleting.

title: Wishlist
goal: Each person manages the gifts they would like (table wishes).

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• add_wish(db, participant_id, title, price=None, url="", priority=2): return the new id. ValueError if the title is empty, the price is negative, or the priority is not 1, 2 or 3. The price may be None (unknown).
  • list_wishes(db, participant_id): most wanted first (priority 1 first), then by title.
  • delete_wish(db, wish_id).
  • wishlist_total(wishes): sum of the known prices; wishes without a price are skipped.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A form for the person chosen in "I am", their list with delete buttons, and a metric comparing the total to the group's budget.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: find(..., order_by=["priority", "title"]) sorts for you. wishlist_total receives the rows already loaded: no database inside, just a loop and an if.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Warn when the total is above the budget. Show the link as a clickable URL. Sort by price.

title: Gift catalogue
goal: Browse a list of gift ideas and keep favorites.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• CATALOGUE: a list of at least 12 dictionaries with exactly the keys name, category and price ({"name": ..., "category": ..., "price": ...}), spread over several categories.
  • categories(items): the categories, sorted, without duplicates.
  • filter_items(items, category=None, max_price=None): keep one category (None = all) and items costing at most max_price (None = any price, the limit price is included).
  • create_tables(db), add_favorite(db, participant_id, item_name) (adding twice does nothing), list_favorites(db, participant_id) (sorted names).

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A category select and a price slider, the matching items, a "favorite" button on each, and a bar chart of the number of items per category.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: A set removes duplicates. For favorites, check exists(...) before insert(...), or create the table with unique=[("participant_id", "item_name")] and use insert(..., on_conflict="ignore"). st.bar_chart needs a table or a dictionary.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Add a favorite directly to the wishlist. Sort by price.

title: Greeting card
goal: Write a small card to go with the gift, in the right tone.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• TEMPLATES: a dictionary tone → text with {receiver} and {sender} placeholders. Tones: funny, warm, formal.
  • default_tone(kind): work → formal, family → warm, friends → funny (anything else → warm).
  • render_card(tone, receiver, sender): the filled text. ValueError for an unknown tone or an empty name.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: The receiver is the person you give a gift to (read it from assignments for the current participant; if there is no draw, let the user type a name). A tone choice preselected from the group kind, the card in a nice frame, and a download button.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: str.format(receiver=..., sender=...). If you display user text inside HTML, escape it with html.escape first. See st.html and st.download_button.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Save the cards in a table, and let the receiver read and delete the cards they got. Think about the signature: if the card carries the real name of the giver, the secret is gone. How would you sign it instead?

title: Christmas quiz
goal: Answer questions, get a score, compare with the group.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• QUESTIONS: a list of dictionaries {"question": ..., "choices": [...], "answer": ...} (about 8). The answer must be one of the choices.
  • score_answers(answers): number of right answers; answers[i] is the choice for QUESTIONS[i] (it may be None when unanswered).
  • create_tables(db), save_score(db, participant_id, score) (ValueError if the score is below 0 or above the number of questions).
  • leaderboard(db, group_id): one row (name, best score) per player of the group, best first, ties sorted by name.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A form with one st.radio per question (no default answer), a submit button, st.balloons() for a perfect score, and the leaderboard as a chart.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: Get the people of the group with find, then their scores with find(..., {"participant_id": [list of ids]}). Keep the best score of each person in a dictionary (max(...)), use index_by to get names, then sorted(...).

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: A donut chart (right / wrong) for the last attempt. Shuffle the questions. A timer.

title: Gift progress
goal: Each giver tracks where their gift is: idea, bought, wrapped, given.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• STATUSES = ["idea", "bought", "wrapped", "given"].
  • create_tables(db), set_status(db, giver_id, status) (ValueError for an unknown status; replaces the previous one), get_status(db, giver_id) ("idea" if nothing saved).
  • group_progress(db, group_id): how many givers of the group's draw are in each status, as a dictionary that contains every status, with 0 when nobody is in it. No names: the secret stays safe.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: Only for a person who has a receiver: a select to change the status and a progress bar. Under it, a bar chart of the whole group.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: insert(..., on_conflict="replace") keeps one row per giver (make the giver the primary key of your table). Trap: if the select's index depends on the saved value, Streamlit treats it as a new widget after each save and you must click twice. Give the widget a fixed key and save with on_change.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Show the date of the last change. Remind the giver when the deadline is close.

title: Group stats
goal: Numbers and charts about the wishes of a group (read only).

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• wishes_per_person(db, group_id): (name, number of wishes) for everyone, including people with 0.
  • prices(db, group_id): the known prices of all wishes of the group.
  • price_buckets(prices): counts in the ranges "0-10", "10-20", "20-50", "50+". A price of 10 goes in "10-20" (lower bound included).
  • average_price(prices): 0 when there is no price.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A few st.metric, a bar chart of wishes per person, and a bar chart of the price ranges.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: Loop over all the people of the group and call count(db, "wishes", {"participant_id": person["id"]}) for each: someone with 0 wishes is simply counted as 0, nobody is forgotten. For the prices, ask find with {"participant_id": [list of ids]} and skip the None prices.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Most wished-for items. Compare with the other groups.

title: Basic draw
goal: Decide who gives a gift to whom: everybody gives once, receives once, and never to themself.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• make_draw(participant_ids, rng=random): a dictionary giver_id → receiver_id. ValueError if there are fewer than 2 people. With two people the only possible draw is {1: 2, 2: 1}. Use rng (not random directly) for every random choice: the tests pass random.Random(seed) so that the result can be predicted.
  • save_draw(db, group_id, pairs): store the dictionary in the shared assignments table, replacing the previous draw of the group.
  • load_draw(db, group_id): read it back as a dictionary ({} if no draw).

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A "Draw" button. If a draw already exists, ask for a confirmation (a checkbox) before replacing it. st.snow() after a draw. The full list of pairs only inside st.expander("Organizer view").

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: Shuffle a copy of the list and check that nobody is in front of their own id; start again if not. Why is starting again fair? Feature 19 explores exactly that question.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Refuse the draw when a group has fewer than 3 people. Keep a history of previous draws.

title: Exclusion rules
goal: Some pairs (couples, roommates) must not draw each other, in either direction.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• create_tables(db) and your own table for the rules.
  • add_exclusion(db, group_id, person_a, person_b, reason=""): return the new id. ValueError for the same person twice, or for a rule that already exists (a, b and b, a are the same rule).
  • list_exclusions(db, group_id): rows with the keys name_a, name_b and reason (plus what you need).
  • delete_exclusion(db, exclusion_id).
  • is_allowed(giver, receiver, exclusions): exclusions is a set of frozensets, for example {frozenset((1, 2))}. A person is never allowed to give to themself.
  • draw_with_exclusions(participant_ids, exclusions, rng=random, tries=1000): a dictionary giver → receiver that respects every rule, or None if no valid draw is found (or fewer than 2 people).

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A form with two selects, the list of rules with a delete button, a graph of the forbidden pairs with st.graphviz_chart, and a button that draws with the rules and saves it into assignments. A warning when no draw is possible.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: A frozenset is a set that can itself be put in a set, and frozenset((1, 2)) == frozenset((2, 1)). For the draw, try random shuffles up to tries times.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Detect an impossible situation before trying (two people who can only draw each other). Explain which rule is the problem.

title: Reveal with a PIN
goal: Each person chooses a 4-digit PIN, then uses it to discover who they give a gift to, once the draw is done.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• create_tables(db), hash_pin(pin): a text that is not the PIN, always the same for the same PIN, different for different PINs. Use hashlib.sha256. The PIN itself is never stored.
  • set_pin(db, participant_id, pin): exactly 4 digits, otherwise ValueError ("123", "12345", "abcd", "" and "12 4" are all refused). Replaces the previous PIN.
  • check_pin(db, participant_id, pin): true or false; false if the person has no PIN.
  • reveal(db, participant_id, pin): the name of the receiver, or None when the PIN is wrong or there is no draw. It records that the person has revealed.
  • has_revealed(db, participant_id). (You will probably also want has_pin(db, participant_id) for the page.)

sections.title: The page
sections.html: If the person has no PIN, ask them to choose one. Otherwise ask for it and show the receiver in big letters with st.snow(). Show a short note that this is a learning exercise, not real security.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: str.isdigit() and len. hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest().

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Block the reveal after 3 wrong PINs. Show when the person revealed.

title: Import and export CSV
goal: Load participants from a spreadsheet file and export results.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• parse_participants_csv(text): returns (rows, errors). The first line must be the header name,email. Each valid row becomes {"name": ..., "email": ...} with the name stripped and the email lowercased. Each invalid row (empty name, email without @) is skipped and adds a message that starts with Line N (the header is line 1, so the first data row is line 2). A missing header or an empty text returns no rows and one error.
  • import_rows(db, group_id, rows): add the people, skipping the emails already in the group. Return how many were imported.
  • export_participants_csv(db, group_id): CSV text with the header name,email, readable again by your parser.
  • export_draw_csv(db, group_id): CSV text with the header giver,receiver, one line per pair. Without draw, only the header line, followed by a newline.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: st.file_uploader, a preview with st.dataframe, the list of errors, an import button, and download buttons. The draw export goes in the organizer expander.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: The csv module (DictReader, writer) and io.StringIO do the hard work. Test your parser with a file that contains mistakes on purpose.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Accept ; as a separator (Excel in France). Import wishes too.

title: Budget tracker
goal: Each giver notes what they spend and compares it to the group budget, without revealing who gives to whom.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• create_tables(db) and your own table for the expenses.
  • add_expense(db, giver_id, label, amount, today=None): return the new id. The label is stripped and required, the amount must be above 0. The date of the expense is today (default: the real date) stored as 2026-12-01.
  • list_expenses(db, giver_id): oldest first, rows with label, amount, spent_on.
  • group_expenses(db, group_id): all expenses of the group, sorted by date, rows with spent_on and amount.
  • spent_by_giver(db, group_id): a list of (name, total) for everyone in the group, including 0, sorted by name.
  • budget_status(total, budget): "ok", "warning" from 90% of the budget up to and including 100%, "over" above the budget.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A form for the current person, a metric of their total with st.progress, a bar chart of the spending of the group with a line at the budget, and a cumulative line chart over time.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: For each person of the group, sum(...) of the amounts of their expenses (the sum of an empty list is 0, so people who spent nothing are kept). For the cumulative chart, itertools.accumulate or pandas cumsum(). Altair can add a rule line with mark_rule.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Delete an expense. Show how much is left.

title: Reminders
goal: Remind people with an empty wishlist, 7 days and 1 day before the deadline. The "emails" are stored in a table (nothing is really sent).

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• REMINDER_DAYS = {7: "J-7", 1: "J-1"} and create_tables(db) (your own table: the outbox).
  • people_to_remind(db, group_id, today=None): the people with no wish at all, but only if exactly 7 or exactly 1 day is left; otherwise an empty list.
  • build_reminder(name, group_name, days_left): the text. It contains the name, the group name and 7 days; for one day it says 1 day (singular).
  • send_reminders(db, group_id, today=None): store one fake email per person to remind and return the count. The same kind of reminder is never sent twice to the same person, but J-1 can follow J-7.
  • list_outbox(db, group_id): the stored emails, with a kind key (J-7 or J-1).

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A date input "Today" that lets you test without waiting, the number of days left, a send button, the outbox in a table, and a timeline of the deadlines of all groups with a vertical line for today.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: create_table(..., unique=[("participant_id", "kind")]) plus insert(..., on_conflict="ignore") prevents duplicates, and insert returns None when the row was not added: count only the others. The deadlines of the demo groups are fixed on the day the database is created, so use the "Today" input to travel to day J-7.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Send a real email (ask a mentor: it needs a test mail server, never use real addresses). Explain on the page why nobody was reminded.

title: Santa sheet
goal: A printable page for each giver: who they give to, the wishes, the budget and the deadline.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• build_sheet_html(giver, receiver, wishes, budget, deadline): a complete HTML page as text. It starts with <!DOCTYPE html>, contains <meta charset="utf-8"> (so accents work), the two names, each wish title with its price formatted like 12.00 €, the budget like 20.00 € and the deadline. Every value is escaped (<script> must come out as <script>, A & B as A & B). wishes is a list of dictionaries {"title": ..., "price": ...}; a price may be None. Without wishes the page says No wish yet.
  • sheet_data(db, giver_id): a dictionary with exactly the keys giver, receiver (names), wishes (the receiver's wishes), budget and deadline, or None if there is no draw.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A preview with st.html for the current person and a download button for the .html file. In the organizer expander, one download per participant.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: html.escape. An f-string for the page, and a for loop for the wishes.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: A nicer layout with CSS, a print stylesheet (@media print).

title: Guess your Santa
goal: Everyone guesses who their Santa is, and the page tells who was right.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• create_tables(db) and your own table for the guesses (one guess per person).
  • save_guess(db, participant_id, guessed_id): ValueError if you guess yourself. A new guess replaces the previous one.
  • guess_results(db, group_id): one dictionary per guess, with name, guessed (names), santa (the real Santa's name, or None if there is no draw) and correct (True or False, never None).
  • score(results): the number of correct guesses (0 for an empty list).

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A select with the other people, and the results only after the user ticks "Reveal results". Show the score and a donut chart (right / wrong). The detailed table, which gives the whole draw away, goes in the organizer expander.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: find_one(db, "assignments", {"group_id": ..., "receiver_id": <the person who guesses>}) gives the pair, and its giver_id is the real Santa; index_by turns ids into names. A person who has not been drawn has no pair: handle None. Altair's mark_arc draws a donut.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: A leaderboard of the best detectives across the quiz.

title: Chain draw
goal: One single loop A → B → C → ... → A. Never two small loops (A ↔ B and C ↔ D).

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• make_chain(participant_ids, rng=random): a dictionary giver → receiver forming one loop that visits everybody. ValueError below 2 people.
  • is_single_chain(pairs): True if, starting from anybody and following giver → receiver, you visit every person exactly once before coming back to the start. {1: 2, 2: 1, 3: 4, 4: 3} is not a single chain.
  • chain_with_exclusions(participant_ids, exclusions, rng=random): a single chain where no pair of the exclusions (a set of frozensets, as in feature 10) is used, or None when impossible. Hint: backtracking.
  • chain_to_dot(pairs, names): a Graphviz text that draws the chain as a circle. It must contain circo and one arrow per pair like "Alice" -> "Bob". names maps an id to a name.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A button that draws and saves into assignments. The graph (st.graphviz_chart) only in the organizer expander.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: Shuffle the list, then give each person to the next one, and the last one to the first. For is_single_chain, walk through the pairs counting the steps. For backtracking: build the chain person by person; when the next person is forbidden, try another one; if nobody fits, go back one step and change the previous choice. Write the recursion on paper first.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Show the chain in the page as "A → B → C → A" text. Count how many chains exist for 5 people.

title: Weighted draw
goal: Each Santa rates how well they know the others (0 to 3), and the draw gives them, as much as possible, someone they know well.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• create_tables(db) and your own table for the ratings.
  • set_affinity(db, giver_id, receiver_id, score): ValueError if the score is outside 0 to 3 or if giver and receiver are the same person. A new score replaces the old one.
  • get_affinities(db, group_id): a dictionary (giver, receiver) → score with an entry for every ordered pair of two different people of the group (4 people give 12 entries), 0 when not rated.
  • total_score(pairs, scores): the sum of the scores of the pairs of a draw.
  • greedy_draw(participant_ids, scores): each giver, in the order of the list, takes the free receiver with the best score. The result must always be a valid draw, even in the corner case where the last giver would be left with only themself (then swap with another giver). scores is a dictionary; a missing pair counts for 0.
  • best_draw(participant_ids, scores): try every possible draw and keep the best total. ValueError above 8 people (too slow).
  • random_score(participant_ids, scores, rng=random, runs=200): the average total score of plain random draws (0 when there is no score).

sections.title: The page
sections.html: The current person rates the others with sliders. A heatmap of all ratings (organizer expander). A bar chart that compares the total score of a random draw, of the greedy draw and of the best draw. A button that saves the greedy draw in assignments.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: itertools.permutations lists all the orders of a list. A draw where nobody gives to themself is a permutation with no fixed point. Is greedy always the best? Find a counterexample with 3 people, then check that your best_draw finds a better result.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Let the group see the average satisfaction without names.

title: Fair draw
goal: Prove with numbers and charts that shuffling and starting again is fair, and that a "natural" method is not.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• A draw is a tuple of receivers: draw[i] is the receiver of ids[i].
  • all_derangements(ids): the list of all possible draws where nobody gives to themself (4 people give 9).
  • random_derangement(ids, rng=random): shuffle everybody, start again if someone got themself.
  • biased_derangement(ids, rng=random): the naive method. Each giver in turn picks randomly among the receivers still free (not themself). If the last giver is left with themself, start again.
  • simulate(draw_function, ids, runs, rng=random): run the draw runs times, return a collections.Counter of how many times each draw came out.
  • naive_probabilities(ids): the exact chance of each draw with the naive method, by maths and not by simulation. Together they add up to 1.
  • uniformity_score(counter, draws): the chi-square statistic divided by the number of possible draws minus 1. It is about 1 when luck alone explains the counts, much bigger when a draw is favoured. ValueError with fewer than 2 possible draws.
  • pair_frequencies(counter, ids): (giver, receiver) → share of the draws where this giver gives to this receiver.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A slider for the number of draws, the uniformity score of both methods, one chart with all the possible draws and both methods, and two heatmaps giver × receiver.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: For naive_probabilities: the chance of a draw is the product, over the givers, of 1 / (number of choices the giver had). Then divide by the total so that the runs that start again are taken into account. Chi-square: the sum over all possible draws of (observed - expected)² / expected, where expected = runs / number of possible draws. Do not forget the draws that never came out: they count with an observed value of 0.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Find another naive method that is even more biased. Explain in two sentences why the naive method favours some draws.

title: Secret messages
goal: An anonymous conversation between a Santa and the person they give to.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• create_tables(db) and your own table for the messages.
  • santa_pseudonym(giver_id): a funny name (elf names in a list of your choice) that depends only on the id: always the same for the same Santa, different for different ids.
  • my_receiver(db, group_id, participant_id) and my_santa(db, group_id, participant_id): the id of the person I give to / the person who gives to me, or None when there is no draw.
  • send_message(db, group_id, sender_id, recipient_id, body): allowed only between a Santa and their receiver, in both directions. ValueError for anybody else, without draw, for an empty message, or for more than 500 characters.
  • conversation(db, group_id, a, b): the messages between the two people (both directions), oldest first, with a body key. Messages with other people never appear.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: Two tabs: "To my receiver" (I write under my pseudonym) and "From my Santa" (my Santa appears only under their pseudonym, never with their real name). Use st.chat_message and st.chat_input.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: The modulo operator % gives a stable choice from a list. A message is allowed if (sender, recipient) or (recipient, sender) is a pair of assignments.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Refresh the conversation every few seconds. Read the verdict of feature 21 before sending (what would you need to share code between features?).

title: Spoiler check
goal: Before sending a message, check whether it gives away who you are, with simple rules (no AI).

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• check_message(text, santa_name): returns (verdict, reasons).
  • "block" if the message contains the Santa's name as a whole word, ignoring case and accents (CHLOE matches Chloé, but malice does not match Alice), or an email address.
  • "warn" for signature phrases (it's me, signed, from your, love,, xoxo, in any case) or an initial like - A..
  • "send" with an empty list of reasons otherwise.
  • When there is a block, the verdict is "block", and the reasons keep all the problems found, warnings included.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A text area, the Santa's name (default: the current participant), a colored result (st.success, st.warning, st.error) and the list of reasons.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text) splits é into e plus an accent, which you can then remove. re.search with \b matches whole words. re.escape protects special characters of a name. Write the regular expression for the email on a small separate test first.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Think about what your rules miss ("a friend who works near you"). Which rule would catch it, and what false alarms would it create?

title: My dashboard
goal: One person (same email) can be in several groups. Show all of them on one page.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• my_groups(db, email, today=None): one dictionary per group where this email is a participant, sorted by deadline (closest first), with the keys group (the name), kind, deadline, days_left, receiver (the name of the person I give to, or None without draw) and wishes (how many wishes I have in this group).
  • next_deadline(rows): the first row whose deadline is today or later, or None.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: The email of the current participant, a card per group with its icon (database.KINDS), metrics, and a timeline of the deadlines with a line for today.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: The email is the link between participants of different groups: find(db, "participants", {"email": email}) gives one row per group. For each row, look up the group, the draw and the wishes with find_one and count. A loop is fine: simple and slow is better than clever and wrong. Clean the email first (strip, lower).

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Highlight the closest deadline. Warn about groups where my wishlist is empty.

title: Admin dashboard
goal: The health of every group at a glance.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• groups_health(db, today=None): one dictionary per group, closest deadline first, with the keys id, name, kind, participants (count), empty_wishlists (people with no wish; someone with two wishes counts as one filled wishlist), drawn (True or False) and days_left. A group with nobody gives 0, 0, False.
  • health_label(row): row is a dictionary with at least drawn, empty_wishlists and days_left. Returns "ready" (drawn and no empty wishlist, even one day before the deadline), "urgent" (not ready, and 7 days or less left or the deadline passed), "attention" otherwise.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: Metrics for the whole app, a table (st.dataframe) with a colored label, and a stacked bar chart per group (filled / empty wishlists).

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: find(db, "groups", order_by="deadline"), then for each group: find its participants, count those with no wish (exists), and ask exists on assignments to know whether a draw was made. Build one dictionary per group.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Sort by urgency. An "export to CSV" button.

title: Time machine
goal: Record every change of the participants and wishes in a history, then replay it with a slider.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• create_tables(db): creates your log table and SQLite triggers (see CREATE TRIGGER in the SQLite documentation) that write into the log whenever a row of participants or wishes is inserted or deleted.
  • history(db, group_id): the events of the group in the order they happened, with the keys table_name ("participants" or "wishes"), action ("insert" or "delete") and your data.
  • replay(events, step): apply the first step events and return {"participants": [names], "wishes": [titles]}. With step=0, both lists are empty.

The triggers must never make an insert or a delete fail, and the tests check hard cases: deleting a participant who has wishes, and deleting a whole group (wishes and participants disappear automatically).

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A slider over the steps, the state of the group at that step, and a chart of the number of events over time. Explain on the page that only changes made after the first visit are recorded.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.html:
This is the one feature that needs real SQL (a trigger is a rule written inside the database). Ask a mentor for a 15-minute introduction, and read CREATE TRIGGER. You write the trigger with db.execute(...); reading the log back works with find. json_object('id', NEW.id, 'name', NEW.name) builds JSON inside SQL. NEW and OLD are the row inserted / deleted. Think about the order of events when deleting a participant with wishes, and about the moment at which you can still find the group of a wish.

Be careful: the triggers stay in the database file once created, and then record the changes made by every other page. If something strange happens in another feature, delete app/data/app.db and start again.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Record who made the change. A "restore this state" button (discuss the risks with your mentor first).

title: Draw history
goal: Keep the draw of each year and draw again without giving the same person to the same Santa.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• create_tables(db) and your own tables (a saved draw with a label, and its pairs).
  • save_snapshot(db, group_id, label, today=None): store the current draw (table assignments) under a label such as "2025", and return its id. ValueError for an empty label, a label already saved in this group, or when there is no draw. today is the saving date.
  • list_snapshots(db, group_id) (most recent first), delete_snapshot(db, snapshot_id).
  • snapshot_pairs(db, snapshot_id): the saved draw as a dictionary giver → receiver.
  • past_pairs(db, group_id, last=None): the set of (giver, receiver) of all saved draws, or only of the last most recent ones.
  • save_draw(db, group_id, pairs): replace the draw of the group in assignments.
  • draw_avoiding(participant_ids, forbidden, rng=random): a dictionary giver → receiver where nobody draws themself and no pair of forbidden (a set of (giver, receiver)) is used, or None if impossible (also under 2 people). When a solution exists, it must be found: the tests include a case with a single solution.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A form to save the current draw, the list of saved draws (with a table and a delete button), and a "Draw" button with a confirmation that avoids the last N saved draws.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: Random shuffles can miss a rare solution. Think of the draw as matching each giver with a free receiver: when a receiver is already taken, ask the giver who has it to look for another one (a recursive "try to move" function).

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Also respect the rules of feature 10. Show which pairs repeated when a draw is impossible.

title: ICS calendar
goal: Download the dates of a group as an .ics file, to add them to any calendar.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• group_events(group, party_day=None): a list of events. group is a dictionary with id, name, deadline (text 2026-12-20) and budget. An event is a dictionary with uid, summary, day (a date), description and alarms (days before the event). The deadline gives one event with alarms at 7 and 1 days; a party_day adds a second event.
  • escape(text): escape \, ;, , and new lines as the ICS format requires (, becomes \,).
  • fold(line): cut a line into pieces of at most 75 bytes (UTF-8, so é counts for 2), each next piece starting with a space, joined with \r\n.
  • build_ics(events, now=None): the text of the file, with \r\n line endings, from BEGIN:VCALENDAR to END:VCALENDAR. Each event is an all-day event (DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20261220, and DTEND is the next day), has a DTSTAMP built from now (UTC, like 20261101T100000Z) and a VALARM with TRIGGER:-P7D for each alarm.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: The events, an optional party date, and st.download_button with the mime type text/calendar.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: Read the format in RFC 5545 (sections 3.1 and 3.3.11 are enough), or open an .ics file exported from your own calendar. date.strftime("%Y%m%d") or an f-string with {day:%Y%m%d}.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Add the deadlines of all the groups of one email (see feature 22). Import your file in a calendar and look at the reminders.

title: Teams
goal: Put the people of a group in teams: a couple, the children, a household.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• create_tables(db) and your own tables. A person is in one team at most.
  • create_team(db, group_id, name): return the id. The name is stripped. ValueError for an empty name or a name already used in this group.
  • add_member(db, team_id, participant_id): put the person in the team. If they were in another team, they move. ValueError if the person is not in the group of the team.
  • remove_member(db, participant_id), delete_team(db, team_id) (the members stay in the group, without team).
  • list_teams(db, group_id): a list of {"id", "name", "members": [participant ids]}, sorted by team name.
  • team_of(db, group_id): a dictionary {participant id: team id} (only people who have a team).

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A form to create a team, and for each team its members, a select to add someone, buttons to remove a member or delete the team.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: If the participant id is the primary key of your members table, insert(..., on_conflict="replace") moves a person for you. Deleting a person or a team must not leave members behind: ON DELETE CASCADE.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: A role per team ("parents", "children"). Warn about people without a team.

title: Group gifts
goal: The core draw gives one receiver to each giver. A group gift has several givers and several receivers: the children together for both parents, each parent for each child... The shared table assignments is not touched.
needs: none (27 is optional on the page)

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• create_tables(db) and your own tables (gifts, givers, receivers). A gift has a source text ("manual" by default).
  • create_gift(db, group_id, label, giver_ids, receiver_ids, source="manual"): return the id. The label is stripped and a person given twice counts once. ValueError for an empty label, no giver or no receiver, someone who is both giver and receiver of the same gift, or someone outside the group.
  • create_each_to_each(db, group_id, giver_ids, receiver_ids): one gift per (giver, receiver), labelled "Alice → Bob", skipping a person giving to themself. Return the ids. ValueError if there is nothing to create.
  • list_gifts(db, group_id): a list of {"id", "label", "source", "givers": [ids], "receivers": [ids]} (ids sorted). A gift left without giver or without receiver (people deleted) is not listed.
  • gifts_to_give(db, group_id, participant_id): the gifts where this person is a giver. A receiver never sees a gift for them.
  • delete_gift(db, gift_id), delete_by_source(db, group_id, source).

sections.title: The page
sections.html: "Gifts I give" for the current person (with the co-givers). The creation form and the full list only in st.expander("Organizer view"). If feature 27 exists, offer whole teams as a shortcut to choose givers or receivers.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: One table for the gifts and one table for each side keeps the model simple: (gift_id, participant_id). Check the people before inserting anything, so a refused gift leaves no half-created rows.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Warn when someone gives a lot more gifts than the others. Show "who gives what" as a graph.

title: Unit draw
goal: A draw where teams count, like exclusion rules but for whole teams. Needs 25 and 28 for the logic, and 27 for the page (the teams).
needs: 25 and 28 (27 for the page)

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• forbidden_pairs(participant_ids, team_of, mode): the set of (giver, receiver) a mode forbids. team_of is {participant id: team id}. Mode "across": nobody draws someone of their own team (people without a team have no restriction). Mode "within": people only draw someone of their own team (people without a team stay together). ValueError for another mode.
  • draw_people(participant_ids, team_of, mode, past=(), rng=random): a draw giver → receiver that follows the mode and avoids the pairs of past, or None. Reuse draw_avoiding of feature 25.
  • make_units(participant_ids, team_of): the list of units: one list of ids per team, and one for each person without team.
  • draw_units(participant_ids, team_of, rng=random): a list of {"givers": [...], "receivers": [...]}: each unit gives one shared gift to another unit, and every unit receives once. None with fewer than two units.
  • save_units(db, group_id, gifts): store the result with the group gifts of feature 28, with the source "unit_draw". A new unit draw replaces the previous one of the group, it never piles up.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: Three kinds of draw (across, within, units), a checkbox to avoid the pairs of the draw history, a confirmation before replacing a result, and the result in st.expander("Organizer view").

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: A unit is only an id: once units are numbered, a draw between units is a draw between people. The draw between people is saved with save_draw, so all the other features keep working.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Also respect the exclusion rules of feature 10. Give the budget of a unit gift: the budget of the group times the number of givers.

title: Gift split
goal: Set the price of a group gift and decide how much each giver pays. Needs 28.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• create_tables(db) and your own tables (a price per gift, a share per giver). Amounts are integer cents.
  • to_cents(amount): 19.99 → 1999 (and 0.1 + 0.2 → 30). format_amount(cents): 1999 → "19.99 €".
  • equal_shares(price_cents, giver_ids): {giver: cents} that always adds up to the price; the extra cents go to the first givers sorted by id (1000 between 3 people: 334, 333, 333).
  • set_price(db, gift_id, price_cents): save the price and give every giver an equal share. ValueError for a price of 0 or less, or an unknown gift.
  • set_shares(db, gift_id, shares): {giver: cents}. ValueError without price, with someone who is not a giver, with a negative amount, or when the total is not the price. Givers who are not in shares pay 0.
  • get_split(db, gift_id): {"price_cents", "shares": {giver: cents}}, or None without price.
  • person_totals(db, group_id): {person: cents they pay for all the gifts of the group}.
  • shares_over_budget(db, group_id): the shares above the budget of the group (the limit itself is fine), as {"label", "participant_id", "amount_cents"}. The budget is in euros in groups.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: For the gifts the current person gives: a price field, an "equal split" button, a field per giver and a "Save the shares" button that shows the error message. Totals and warnings in the organizer view.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: divmod(price, number_of_people) gives the base share and the number of extra cents. round(amount * 100).

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Mark who has paid. Propose a split proportional to something (income, wishlist...).

title: Gift pool
goal: Everybody in a group except one person chips in for that person's gift. The person sees nothing before the due date, then discovers the amount collected.

sections.title: Write in logic.py
sections.html:
• create_tables(db) and your own tables (the pools, the contributions). One pool per person and per group. Amounts are integer cents.
  • to_cents(amount) and format_amount(cents), as in feature 30 (copy them: this feature is independent).
  • is_open(pool, today=None): contributions are possible until the day before the due date; on the due date the pool is closed.
  • create_pool(db, group_id, creator_id, receiver_id, title, target_cents, due_date, today=None): return the id. target_cents can be None (no target). ValueError for an empty title, a creator who is the receiver, people outside the group, a target of 0 or less, a due date that is not in the future, or a person who already has a pool.
  • contribute(db, pool_id, participant_id, amount_cents, today=None): a new contribution replaces the previous one of the same person (it is not added). ValueError for the receiver, someone outside the group, an amount of 0 or less, or a closed pool.
  • withdraw(db, pool_id, participant_id, today=None): remove a contribution while the pool is open. delete_pool(db, pool_id, participant_id): only the creator can.
  • visible_pools(db, group_id, viewer_id): the pools of the group except the one for the viewer, each with contributions ({person: cents}) and total_cents.
  • received_pool(db, group_id, viewer_id, today=None): the pool for the viewer once the due date is reached, otherwise None. Before that date the person must not learn that a pool exists.

sections.title: The page
sections.html: A form to start a pool, the pools you can chip in (progress bar if there is a target, a field and buttons), and, for the current person, a celebration with the total and the names of the contributors (no individual amounts) once the pool is received.

sections.title: Hints
sections.html: The secret is kept in logic.py, not only on the page: visible_pools and received_pool decide who sees what, and the tests check it. To compare dates, date.fromisoformat.

sections.title: Going further
sections.html: Thank-you message from the receiver. Suggest a share (target divided by the number of possible contributors). Warn when the due date is close and the target is far.
